target.name: Carbon dioxide, captured at cement production plant, with heat recovery, for subsequent reuse

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: Table 59 'Life-cycle inventories of the different carbon dioxide capture systems', column 'carbon dioxide, captured at cement production plant, for subsequent reuse/CH U', with-heat-recovery variant; per 1 kg CO2; allocation: none stated. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2024 - LCA power-to-X in residential sector - Sacchi.pdf

gaps_reported_by_model: No capture-unit infrastructure is booked for the cement (or MSWI) columns - only the DAC column carries the plant (concrete, steel, hall, collector containers) and its end-of-life.
No 'Carbon dioxide, in air' uptake resource: that appears only in the DAC column; the CO2 captured here comes from the kiln's flue gas and is not booked as a flow.
No ammonia emission for the cement column (the MSWI column has 1.00e-04 kg).
The electricity figure of Tab. 59 (6.90e-03 kWh/kg) contradicts Tab. 58 (0.07 MWh/t = 0.07 kWh/kg) by a factor of ten.
No compression or conditioning of the captured CO2 for reuse.
